summary:
A queue can rotate: move the front to the back, repeatedly. After adding a new item at the back, rotate the
`size − 1` older items behind it, and the new item sits at the front. The queue is then always in stack order,
so `pop` and `top` just use the front. `push` is O(n), everything else O(1).

question.md:
Implement a stack (`push`, `pop`, `top`, `empty`) with a single queue and only queue operations: add to the back,
look at or remove the front, size, is-empty.

- **A queue gives back the oldest item; a stack must give back the newest.**
- **One queue only**, no second container.
- **At most 3000 calls**, so O(n) per call is acceptable.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Only queue operations are allowed: add to the back, read/remove the front.
- Interleaved pushes and pops.
- `pop`/`top` only on a non-empty stack.

think.md:
**Amortised cost.** Some operations occasionally do a lot of work (pouring a whole stack, rotating a whole queue). What
matters is the total over many operations: if each item can only be moved a constant number of times overall, the
average per operation is O(1), even if one particular call is slow.

**Rotation.** Removing the front and adding it to the back keeps the cyclic order of a queue. So after adding a
new item at the back, rotating `size − 1` times brings it to the front, while everything else keeps its order
behind it. If every push does that, the front is always the newest item: the stack's top.

approaches.title: Rotate when reading

idea.md: Push to the back. For `pop`/`top`, rotate `size − 1` times so the newest item reaches the front, read it (and for `top`, put it back at the end).

build: Rotate the newest to the front on reads.

lines.text: One queue, items in arrival order.

notes.java: `ArrayDeque` used strictly as a queue: `offer` at the back, `poll` from the front.
notes.python: `deque` used strictly as a queue: `append` at the back, `popleft` from the front.

lines.text: Move everything except the newest from the front to the back; the newest is now at the front.
Remove the newest. The remaining items are still in arrival order (just rotated), so the next read works the same way.
Read the newest, then put it back at the back, which restores arrival order exactly.

complexity.md: **Time O(1)** push, **O(n)** pop and top. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: top(): rotate so the newest (3) is at the front, read it, then send it to the back too, restoring the order.
pop(): rotate 2 item(s) to the back so the newest (3) is at the front; remove it.
pop(): rotate 2 item(s) to the back so the newest (4) is at the front; remove it.
top(): rotate so the newest (2) is at the front, read it, then send it to the back too, restoring the order.
Each pop or top rotated almost the whole queue.

walk.title: Keep items in arrival order (newest at the back). To reach the top, rotate everything in front of it to the back.

limits.md: Every read rotates the whole queue. Rotating once per push keeps the queue in stack order, so reads are O(1).

approaches.title: Rotate after every push

idea.md:
On `push`, add the item to the back and rotate `size − 1` times so it's at the front. Then `pop` and `top`
read the front.

**Invariant.** The queue, front to back, lists the items from newest to oldest.

build: Push: add, then rotate the rest behind it.

lines.text: One queue, kept in stack order: front = top.

notes.python: `deque` used strictly as a queue: `append`, `popleft`, and reading `[0]`.

lines.text: The new item joins at the back.
Move every older item from the front to the back, behind the new one. The new item is now at the front, and the older ones keep their newest-first order behind it.
The front is the top of the stack.

complexity.md: **Time O(n)** push, **O(1)** pop and top. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: push(1): add at the back, then move the 0 older item(s) from the front to the back. 1 is now at the front.
push(2): add at the back, then move the 1 older item(s) from the front to the back. 2 is now at the front.
push(3): add at the back, then move the 2 older item(s) from the front to the back. 3 is now at the front.
push(4): add at the back, then move the 2 older item(s) from the front to the back. 4 is now at the front.
Pushes cost O(n); pops and tops are O(1).

walk.title: Keep the queue in stack order: newest at the front. Each push adds at the back and then rotates everything older behind it.

takeaways.md:
- **Stack from a queue:** rotate after each push so the newest item is at the front.
- Choose which operation pays: here pushes are O(n), reads O(1).
- **Pitfall:** rotating `size` times (the new item ends up at the back again).
